 Summary: the tech stack is real (you can absolutely wire Claude into Yahoo Finance/news APIs to track Greeks, theta decay, and alerts — that part's just software). But the 155% claim is a single cherry-picked 30-day window during a rally, with no drawdown data, no multi-month track record, and no way to verify the account. LEAPS + small-cap longs are leveraged directional bets — they look brilliant in an up month and get wrecked in a flat/down one. Also worth noting: this is a funnel into a paid community, so the performance claim is doing marketing work, not proof-of-concept work. The "Claude picked the trades" framing oversells it too — there's no proprietary edge there, just LLM reasoning over public data dressed up as a system. The dashboard/monitoring layer is legitimately useful; the "AI found me the winning trades" narrative is the part to be skeptical of.
